steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: What is it, Morte?

steps.name: Morte
steps.text: (Lies limply on the sofa.)

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: You're still hungry?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Today is a holiday, everyone's having fun.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Even the evil spirits are hiding.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: I saw so many people crying while I got my food at the banquet.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Can't you eat those?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Maybe you're getting picky.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: This morning, the Doctor told me there would be a banquet here.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: There would be food, friends, and all kinds of things we don't usually get—

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: You're asking me if I'm happy?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: I... don't understand.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: The emotions in this place are too strange.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: They've been so rich lately.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: I don't understand some of them.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Like what we saw just now, laughing and drinking.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Talking for a while, then unstoppable tears.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Laughing and crying.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: The combination of joy and sadness makes my head hurt.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Nnn, this is also the only thing I understand.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Morte wouldn't like these emotions.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Another rip?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Okay, it's not that bad.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Get some apples for me, I'll get the other materials.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Go on, don't let the stuffing in your tummy fall out.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Don't wave your knife around either. Doctor will get mad.

steps.name: Morte
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Go on.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Ah, am I disturbing you, Shamare?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: What's wrong?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: I-I just saw you writing for a long time without actually writing anything, so I got curious...

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Am I bothering... your work?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: I'm sorry!

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Um, well, I just finished eating and want to read here... May I?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Thanks, Shamare! Hehe.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Phew, I should be able to let down all my tails on this big sofa— Alright.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Aah... that's better~

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Woo~~

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: You're back?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: (Whispering) Morte, give an apple to Suzuran.

steps.name: Morte
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Haa—

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Eh, Morte?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Is this... for me?!

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Thank you, Shamare!

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Thank you, Morte!

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Wuh?!

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: It's sweet!

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Mmm.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: It's sweet and sour. The temperature is just right, a little cold but not cold enough to hurt my teeth.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Nnnnnng—

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Haa— So happy~

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Ah, I should keep the apple core and find a rubbish bin later.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Morte, are you going to pitch it for me?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Okay, here.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Shamare, aren't you eating?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Later.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: I won't bother you then.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: I'll be reading here.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Hmm—Last time I got to—

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Here.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: 'Dusk Beauty Flying to the Moon'.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Once upon a time, there was a gentle and kind girl named Dusk Beauty who lived in Yan——'

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: (Diligently reads the story, one word at a time).

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: (Puts her pen down).

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Morte, apple.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: (Slowly gnaws on the apple).

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: ——To commemorate the distant Dusk Beauty, on the same day every year, people would offer up her favorite food. As time passed, this day became an important festival in Yan.'

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: So that's where it comes from—
So that's where it comes from—

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Eh?! Popukar? And Miss Mousse?

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Hiya.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Hello, Suzuran.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Why are you all here and not at the banquet? There's a lot of delicious food from Yan there.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: I'm already full. I saw Suzuran telling stories on my way back to the dorm, so I came over to listen.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: I also came to hear the story! And also, um, to look after the kitties. They're getting rambunctious.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Kitties?

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: They're over there...

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: There? Shamare?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Ah, it's true!

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The kitties really like Shamare and Morte!

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Kitties
steps.text: Meow~Purrr—

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: (Tugs on Suzuran's sleeve).

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: That story just now, could you tell it again, Suzuran?

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: I came late and missed some of it.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Me too...

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Ah— Okay!

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Um, it might take a long time to read the whole thing again, so I'll summarize.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: This is a fairy tale from Yan. The protagonist is a girl named Dusk Beauty.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: She was living a happy life with her husband.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Until one day, her husband went missing.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: She must have been very sad.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Yes, the book says Dusk Beauty searched everywhere for her husband, but no one knew where he was.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: She went home and cried under the willow tree her husband had planted himself.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: A wise elder in the village saw Dusk Beauty weeping everyday and came up with an idea.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The old man said—

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: *Cough* *cough*... Mhmm.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: 'Child, you have a pair of sharp eyes that can see thousands of miles away. Why not ascend the mountain to the west?'

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: 'From there you can gaze upon the wide earth. Only there will you have a chance to find your husband.'

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Dusk Beauty agreed with the wise elder's suggestion, and decided to leave the town and head to the mountain at the edge of the land.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: This mountain, the tallest of them all, was called Mount T'ien by the people of Yan.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: That sounds so cool.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The meaning of Mount Sky is 'a mountain as tall as the skies.' There is no mountain taller than it in all of Yan.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: After much tribulation, Dusk Beauty reached the mountain peak and looked out over the vast land. But after three days and three nights, even as her eyes reddened from the strain, there was no sign of her husband.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: With years of her effort ending up fruitless, Dusk Beauty could not help but weep, and her tears flowing down the mountain formed a river.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: How sad...

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Mom said I was like that when I cried as a kid.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: *Sigh*.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The surging tears shocked the gods within the mountains. They couldn't believe the river which had appeared out of nowhere.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Upon seeing the source of the river, they were even more surprised. The gods decided to send their leader, the god of Mount Sky, to talk with the girl.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The kind god listened to Dusk Beauty's story and pitied her. Thus, the god of Mount Sky said:

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: 'Lofty heights of Mount Sky, lie yet dwarfed by the twin moons. Ascend thee to the moons, and thy husband shall thee find soon.'

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Oh, sorry. It's sort of poetic and old-tymey, isn't it? Let me explain.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: It means that even though the mountain was very tall, its height could not compare to the twin moons in the sky. So, if she could fly to the moons, she would definitely be able to find her husband.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Dusk Beauty accepted the mountain god's suggestion, and asked for help. After the gods discussed it, they taught her a way...

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: One night, everyone was going about their business as usual, when suddenly, a bright light rose from the western mountains and rushed towards the moon.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: This light became brighter and brighter, brighter and brighter, and at one point it even became brighter than the moon.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Finally, this light landed on the moon, and a big and brilliant sparkle rose out of it. The night sky grew bright, and it was hard to even see the stars.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: (Whisper) Mousse, can we see fireworks like that now?!

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: (Whisper) Of course not!

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Upon seeing such a thing, everyone panicked, thinking it meant something terrible.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: But the elder recalled the story of Dusk Beauty and told everyone this meant she had found her husband. He told them not to be afraid, and to celebrate instead.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The people were convinced, so they brought out their wine and food, and celebrated the departure of Dusk Beauty.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: From then on, everyone would bring food and gather together to feast once a year. They put the foods that Dusk Beauty liked on an altar.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: They did it every year, without fail.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: As time passed, it became a traditional festival.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Even after Dusk Beauty left, the river continued to flow down from Mount Sky, so the people decided to name the river after her, calling it the Dusk River.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Later on, the village slowly developed into a city. The edge of the city was next to the Dusk River, so naturally the city was called Dusk City.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Is that why there's so much yummy food today?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Actually, today is the day of a Higashi festival as well.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The shrines will be very busy today. Dad's always swamped the whole day.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Though the most lively shrine is always Miss Tsukinogi's shrine. They say the god of her shrine is the chief god, so they have a huge festival, with a lot of people.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: People from all over Higashi travel to Miss Tsukinogi's shrine.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Are there similar stories from Higashi then?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: There are.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Well, it's not really a story, it's actually part of the liturgy. Dad's always reciting it during the ceremonies, he even has to dance along with the music at the same time. It's really fun.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The story goes something like this.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: There was once a poor, old couple who lived working in the fields. One day, all of a sudden, a woman descended from the sky.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The woman handed a jeweled pot to the old man. When he opened it, there were more gold and riches than he'd ever seen in his whole life.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The woman asked the old man to accept the treasures, and to help her look for a husband. The treasures would be a gift to the old man in return.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The old man brought the woman home and discussed the matter with his wife. Upon hearing such a thing, she was ecstatic.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Thus, the old couple hired people to repair their home and invited the woman to stay.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Then, they spread the news about the woman looking for a husband.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The news passed quickly from person to person, and soon everyone in Higashi knew about it.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: But the woman was very picky and most of the hopefuls failed to catch her eye. For those that did, she would ask them to retrieve a treasure for her. If they succeeded, she would marry them.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Do the people of the East all marry like that?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: They used to, long ago.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Now... It's hard to say.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: At least, Dad and Mom didn't get married like that.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Mmm, let's continue.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The woman never asked for the same item twice, but no one was able to fulfill her requests.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: 'As long as you can bring me one treasure, I will become your wife.'

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Many ears heard these words.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: But even the important people from the capital couldn't do it.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: There were even five dignitaries from the capital who asked for her hand in marriage, and were only too helpless in the face of her requests.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: One of them even lost his life search of the treasure.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: After that, even though everyone was still interested in the woman, no one dared to court her.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Scary...

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Three brothers, all hunters who lived on a mountain, heard this news and were intrigued.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The eldest and second brother were interested, but the third brother believed it was just a ploy to trick people.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: But he couldn't convince his brothers and so he set out with them to travel to the old man's house.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Unexpectedly, the woman didn't turn them away, and instead gave them her requests.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: 'As long as you can bring me one treasure, I will become your wife.'

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Mhmm.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The woman asked the eldest brother for a never-melting ice crystal, from the far north.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: From the second brother, she asked for an everlasting flame from the south.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: She would marry whoever brought her the treasure first.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Just as the third brother was to listen to his request, the woman fell silent.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Leaving the old man's house, the two brothers found the requests extraordinarily difficult and impossible to complete.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: But neither of them were willing to return to a life of hardship in the mountains.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: After some discussion, they decided on a deadline.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Three years.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: After three years, no matter if they found the treasure or not, they would return to this place.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The third brother told his older brothers not to let the woman bewitch them.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: But his pleas fell on deaf ears and his brothers went their separate ways as soon as they had agreed on the deadline.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Feeling resentful as he was confused by his elders, the third brother left the village as well.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: So, did they find their treasures?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Three years later, the eldest brother and second brother reunited in the village.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Both of them had found their treasures.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Wow, so they could go and get married!

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Over the course of their treasure hunt, the both of them had become famous and important people.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: But they had pledged their loyalty to different lords, in different factions.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: With their treasures in hand, the two brothers led armies that clashed against each other.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The entire village became a battlefield, and with both sides going on the offensive, they both suffered major losses.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Many of the villagers tried to hide or escape. Refusing to leave their piles of riches, the old couple ended up killed along with the rest of the villagers who stayed behind.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: However, there was no sign of the woman.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: In the end, the two brothers died on the very spot they made their agreement three years prior.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: They're brothers, why did they end up fighting each other?!

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: After the leaders died, both sides continued to send reinforcements into the area.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Soldiers were deployed, fortifications were built, fortresses were erected.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The war in that place never ended.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: The two fortresses were combined together and called Nito-jo.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Between the north and south fortresses lies the ruins of the village...

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: And countless dead...

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Of course, normally only the first few parts are recited in the ceremony. The later parts are only enacted during the great ceremonies once every few years.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: As for why the people of Higashi like this story so much, I'm not really sure either.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: The third brother and the sky woman don't come up again?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Oh, they do. Let me think.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Hm, there are a few versions of the ending.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: One says that after the village was destroyed, someone tried looking for the riches in the old man's house, but he found only bones.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: So he told everyone that the woman was a fairy who had descended to Higashi with great expectations of the land below only to see the greed and tyranny of the people. She returned to heaven disappointed.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Another version is that this was a trickster fairy, and it wasn't the first tragedy she caused, and it wouldn't be the last.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: After witnessing the fate of his elder brothers, the third brother decided to avenge them by killing the fairy.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: But he had no way to travel to heaven, and the fairy taunted him from the sky.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: In the end, the third brother became a ghost who wanders around Higashi, forever searching for a way to take revenge against the fairy.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Morte, come here and let me patch you up.

steps.name: Kitties
steps.text: Meow—

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: I think I heard a story like this when I was little...

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Do you know any Victorian fairy tales?

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Nope.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: I don't know many either...

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Let me tell it, then.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Alright, another story!

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: I hope it's a happy story where no one dies this time.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Haha...

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: (Begins patching the hole in Morte).

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: The story goes like this——

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Ahem...

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Once upon a time, there was a rich Victorian kingdom. The king of this country had a pair of twins.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: When they were born, the most respected caster in the country came to congratulate the king on the birth of the prince and princess, and offered a prophecy:

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: 'With the guidance of the divine light, both will have bright futures.'

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: The king was extremely pleased and bequeathed upon the caster many treasures and riches. But when he asked the caster to explain the prophecy, he fell silent and left the castle instead.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Years later, the prince and princess were grown, but the wise king had fallen ill with a terrible sickness and was bedridden. The doctors said it was a terminal illness, and that only the Divine Originium could save the king.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: All the warriors from across the land set out to search for the Originium, including the prince and princess, disguised as adventurers.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: They had to join the quest to save their father.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: The two traveled together, searching the deepest caves and crossing the wildest forests.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: (Miss Mousse has a very different way of speaking when she's telling a story.)

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: They stopped a scheme by an evil witch, they defeated vicious barbarians, all in search of the smallest clue that could lead them to the Originium.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: What an adventure!

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Finally, they had a lead. Following the clues, the brother and sister climbed up a tall mountain. At the mountain peak, they found a monster——

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: ——And its nest, filled to the brim with treasure.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: This monster could soar through the skies. Its scaly armor repelled all manner of weapons, and from its maw it breathed a fearsome flame. The siblings could not even harm it.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: (Stops the needle and thread in her hand).

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: But they were able to use the monster's greed against it, luring it into its own nest.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: There, the two fought against the monster for ages. In the end, the brother fell unconscious from his injuries and the sister was left to face the monster alone.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Unexpectedly, the monster did not press the attack. Instead, it opened its huge mouth asked why they had entered its nest.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: The princess answered the question honestly:

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: She needed the Divine Originium to save her father's life.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: The monster nodded and pointed to the cave full of treasure, giving her permission to look for the Originium herself.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Not long after, her brother woke up. The monster asked the same question.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: The brother gave the same answer as his sister, and the monster let him pass.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: But when faced with treasure that dwarfed even his country's wealth, the brother changed his mind.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: He stuffed his pockets full of treasure and sneaked out of the cave before his sister could notice.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Bad guy!

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: The sister searched through the piles of treasures for a long time before discovering the Divine Originium that seemed rather dull amongst the glow of the other treasures. Carrying out the Originium, she realized that her brother had disappeared.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: She searched through the entire cave and even worked up the courage to ask the monster of her brother's whereabouts, but the monster merely grinned and said nothing.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: If I had a brother like that——!

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Calm down, Popukar! It's just a story!

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Standing on the mountain peak and looking at the two royals in the distance, the monster let out a roar of satisfaction. The Originium crystals on its body shined a divine light that flickered along with the monster's every breath.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: After that, the princess presented the Originium and the king instantly recovered his vitality.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: He granted a great reward to the princess and even gave her a necklace made from the Divine Originium. Alas, even after the king was cured, he continued to grow.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: More limbs, a larger brain! The king eventually turned into a monster and began slaughtering people indiscriminately!

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: The country's knights banded together and killed the monstrous king. The princess was also charged and sent to the gallows.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: The Originium necklace around her neck shined with a gentle light up until her death.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: In the chaos, the old caster who gave the prophecy to the king all those years ago appeared before the princess and her Divine Originium, only to whisk them away.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: With the end of the royal bloodline, the entire country fell into chaos.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: What about the bad guy brother?!

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: In another country far, far away, the brother heard what happened.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Though he shed tears of guilt, he continued to cram his gullet with the finest foods in the world.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: With the wealth he took from the monster's cave, he had become a noble in another land, and lived out his days in luxury.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: That's unfair!

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Oh, I get it.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Fairy tales are all monsters that eat all the good people.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Shamare is from Siracusa, right? Are there any similar stories over there?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: (Continues sewing Morte).

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: ...Umm, what about you, Suzuran?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Long ago, there was a tribe that lived in a valley surrounded by seven hills.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: The leader of the tribe, She-wolf, had six children.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Each of them took one of the hills, and fought against each other for food.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: A hundred years later, each child had established their own tribe, and the fighting continued as before.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: One of the tribes could not defeat the others, and went to snatch food from She-wolf.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Not wanting to fight her own child, She-wolf leapt into the sky and became the Moonshadow.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Whenever the moon is covered in black, all Lupos should remember the graciousness and rage of She-wolf.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: So that's where the Moonshadow came from.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: The other tribes came to their senses after losing She-wolf.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: They exiled the worst of them, and made some rules.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: From then on, Lupos stopped separating themselves into tribes, and called each other family instead.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Six families each took one hill, with the last dedicated to She-wolf.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Any Lupo who broke the rules would be severely punished by the Sette Colli Council and Sette Colli City.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Does this city still exist?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: But this city was taken over by a larger family a hundred years ago.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Only the story and the rules were passed on.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: The end.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: You guys go ahead.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: (Continues sewing Morte).

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Umm...

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: You all told such good stories, I wanna share one too.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: It's a story Orchid told me.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Can I?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Of course, go ahead!

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Yes, you can do it!

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Let me think...

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Once upon a time, there was a really amazing, umm, wax figure... Right, wax figure!

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: (Whisper) Did she mess up?

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: (Whisper) Let's just listen for now.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: (Whisper) Okay.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: (Continues sewing Morte).

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: The wax figure could make lots of stuff. Everyone called him a great inventor.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: But the wax figure was always very sad.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: He wanted to find a Forte to match with.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Lots of people brought their daughters to him, but he didn't like any of them.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: So the wax figure stayed single.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Until one day! The wax figure realized!

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Since there wasn't a bride for him anywhere in the whole world, he could just make one himself!

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: So he spent a reeeaallly long time, using all his savings.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: And finally, he made a bride!

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: He loved the Forte bride he made a super duper lot, and didn't want anyone else to see her at all.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: (Whisper) Okay, I get it.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: (Whisper) Yeah.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: The king locked the wax figure up and brought his soldiers to the tower, ready to snatch the bride for himself.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: After a couple days, they let the wax figure go.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: He asked people where his bride was, and they told him:

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: When the king and the soldiers went inside the tower, the sky rumbled with thunder and flashed with lightning. Wax oil flowed down from the top of the tower, covering the king and his men.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: The soldiers who escaped said the melted bride was swimming in the wax oil, using wax to kill all the bad guys.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Then the country had no leader, but everyone thought that the wax figure inventor was very smart and asked him to become the new king.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Wait...

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Not wax figure, he was a Forte inventor!

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: They asked the Forte inventor to become the new king!

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Ahhhh...... I got the beginning all wrong...... Should I start over...?

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: It's okay, I understood it all.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Come on, and then what happened?

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: A-And then...?

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Um, and then...

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: And then the inventor became a good king and invented many things. Everyone loved him.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: But he always hid in the palace's garden and never came out.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Because he was trying to make another bride.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: But every time he tried, he failed.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: None of the brides were as perfect as the first bride.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: In the end, the inventor grew old in the garden full of brides and never came out again.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: The people who loved him buried him in the garden, along with all his brides.

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Aww, finally a story with a good ending.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: I asked Orchid where the wax bride went.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: She said the wax bride was stuck in the tower after it collapsed.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: (She probably melted.)

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: But she always wanted to go back to the inventor.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Maybe one day the bride will get to be with her groom again.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: I like warm and fuzzy stories like this.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Popukar, where are you? It's bedtime!

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Orchid, over here!

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Sorry... Orchid says I have to go home and sleep.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: I'll see you again later.

steps.name: Popukar
steps.text: Bye bye!

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: I'm feeling sleepy too...

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Kitties, lets go. Let's not bother Shamare anymore.

steps.name: Kitties
steps.text: Meow—Meoww—

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Stop that, behave.

steps.name: Kitties
steps.text: Meow—

steps.name: Mousse
steps.text: Thanks for the stories, everyone. Good night.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: I should go home too.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Dad will cry if I'm not in bed by ten.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Even though Dad isn't here...

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Aren't you going home, Shamare? It's already very late.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: I still have things to do.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Well then, good night, Shamare.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Good night.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: (Pulls the tear closed).

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Done.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Morte, give me the last apple.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: (Brushes the page using a finger dipped in apple juice).

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: There's the symbol.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Morte, lie on the book.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: The symbol is imprinted and we're done.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Let's go home.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: What's wrong?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Oh, I see it.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Let's give the book back to Suzuran.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: You still want another story?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: That's not like you.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: You're asking why all the stories end like that?

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Think about it, Morte.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Think about our world.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Think about what you eat, and where we used to live.

steps.name: Shamare
steps.text: Does it make sense now?
